# A bounded-hinge full-cardinality cover without individual mass control

Let P be a nonempty finite lattice-convex subset of Z^n, and let
`K_z=[l_z,u_z]` be positive-length interval fibers of an actual convex
family. Put `W=max_z(u_z-l_z)>0`, `M=sum_z(u_z-l_z)`, and
`D_int=[-W,W]`. There exists a cover by at most `2^(n+1)` nonvertical
closed ambient caps for which each positive normalized margin is at
most 1/2 on S. Consequently

    sum_i Psi_Dint(L_i)<=2^n M.

This construction supplies no prescribed individual cap-mass bound.

## Proof

Replace the given convex body by the convex hull of its finitely many
fiber endpoints; this preserves every measured fiber by actual convex
compatibility. For each p in P, there are affine base functions a_p,b_p
with

    a_p(z)<=l_z<=u_z<=b_p(z) for every z in P,
    a_p(p)=l_p, b_p(p)=u_p.

These are finite polyhedral supporting planes. More explicitly, the
finite linear program maximizing `sum_z lambda_z u_z` over probability
weights of mean p has value u_p by compatibility; its dual is the
affine majorant b_p and attains this value. The lower plane is obtained
by the corresponding minimization. This finite-polytope step is needed:
an arbitrary original smooth body can lack a finite-slope support at
a boundary fiber, whereas its endpoint convex hull has these attained
affine planes.

Write `w_p(z)=b_p(z)-a_p(z)`. The closed base halfspaces

    G_p={z:w_p(z)<=W}

cover P because p belongs to G_p. If any w_p is constant with value at
most W, that single set already covers. Otherwise the open complements
are ordinary base halfspaces with common intersection disjoint from P.
Since P is finite, each open complement has the same trace on P as a
closed halfspace obtained by a sufficiently small strict threshold
increase. Relative Doignon therefore extracts at most 2^n of these
complements with empty common trace, equivalently at most 2^n of the
sets G_p that cover P.

For each selected p, use the two ambient margins

    L_p^+(z,x)=x-b_p(z)+W/2,
    L_p^-(z,x)=a_p(z)-x+W/2.

Their sum is `W-w_p(z)`. If z belongs to G_p, this sum is nonnegative,
so at least one margin is nonnegative for every x in K_z. The chosen
pairs thus cover all of S, including all interval endpoints. On every
fiber, the supporting inequalities give

    L_p^+<=W/2,  L_p^-<=W/2.

Both continuous normals have D_int support W. Thus each normalized
positive margin is at most 1/2. Integrating and using the cap count
gives the claimed hinge bound. In fact the proof gives the sharper
identity-level estimate `sum Psi <=(1/2) sum cap_mass`. QED.

## Exact failure of automatic mass-budget preservation

Take `n=d=1`, `P={0,1}`, `K_0=[0,1]`, and `K_1=[0,1/2]`.
This is the actual fiber family of a trapezoid, with `M=3/2`, `W=1`.
The affine supporting pair

    a_0(z)=0, b_0(z)=1-z/2

has `G_0` covering both integer points. Its two strip caps are

    x+z/2-1/2>=0,  1/2-x>=0.

Each has mixed length one, which is `2M/3`. Nevertheless the two
horizontal median caps with margins `x-3/8` and `3/8-x` cover S and
each have mass `3/4=M/2`. Thus the displayed support-strip operation
can violate the budget `tau=1/2` even when a budget-feasible cover
already exists, and even though it uses fewer than the allowed four
caps. This is an obstruction to automatic preservation by this
particular operation, not a counterexample to the existence of some
other bounded-hinge budget-feasible full-cardinality cover.
